Algebraic datatypes

Source: R/datatypes.R
z3_datatype.Rd

Declare new sorts by their constructors, as in functional languages: enumerations, records, lists, trees.

Usage

z3_datatype(ctx, name, ..., parameters = NULL)

z3_datatypes(ctx, specs)

z3_datatype_of(sort)

z3_enum_sort(ctx, name, values)

z3_tuple_sort(ctx, name, ...)

z3_list_sort(ctx, name, element)

z3_tuple_fields(sort)

z3_update_field(x, field, value)

z3_type_variable(ctx, name)

z3_datatype_instance(ctx, name, sort)

z3_is_recursive_datatype(sort)

Arguments

ctx

A z3_context().

name

Name of the datatype.

...

Constructors, each a named list of field sorts. For z3_tuple_sort(), the named field sorts.

parameters

Optional list of type variables.

specs

For z3_datatypes(): a named list whose elements are lists of constructors as in ....

sort

A datatype sort (or a z3_datatype), or sorts for the instance.

values

Names of the enumeration values.

element

Element sort of the list (or a z3_datatype).

x

A value of a datatype.

field

A field accessor (an element of the z3_datatype).

value

New value of the field.

Value

A z3_datatype (a named list of datatypes for z3_datatypes()), a sort for z3_type_variable() and a z3_expr for z3_update_field(). z3_tuple_fields() returns a list with constructor, a z3_function building tuples, and fields, a named list of accessor functions.

Details

z3_datatype(ctx, name, ...) takes one argument per constructor. Each is a named list of fields, mapping field names to sorts; an empty list makes a constructor without fields. A field may refer to the datatype being declared by giving its name as a string, which makes the datatype recursive. z3_datatypes() declares several datatypes at once, so that they can refer to each other (mutual recursion).

The result is a z3_datatype with:

  • $sort: the new sort;

  • one element per constructor: a function building values (or, for a constructor without fields, the value itself);

  • $is_<constructor>: recognizers, true when a value was built by that constructor;

  • one element per field: accessor functions.

z3_enum_sort(), z3_tuple_sort() and z3_list_sort() are shortcuts for the common shapes. z3_enum_sort() and z3_list_sort() use Z3's dedicated constructors.

A datatype name can be declared once per context: Z3 would replace the earlier datatype and free sorts and functions that R objects still use, so z3r refuses a second declaration, also when a script runs again. Keep the earlier object, or use another name or a new context. z3r cannot see datatypes declared by SMT-LIB text (z3_from_smtlib(), z3_eval_smtlib()) or copied in by z3_translate(); do not declare such a name again in that context. z3_tuple_sort() names its constructor mk_<name>. A datatype with a single constructor that has the datatype's own name and no recursive fields, as in z3_datatype(ctx, "Point", Point = list(x = I, y = I)), is declared as a Z3 tuple sort. z3_update_field() returns a copy of a value with one field changed. z3_datatype_of() rebuilds the object from a datatype sort, for example one read from SMT-LIB2. z3_tuple_fields() reads a tuple sort (a datatype with one constructor and no recursive fields): its constructor and its field accessors, in order.

Polymorphic datatypes (Z3 4.15.4 and later) take parameters, a list of type variables made with z3_type_variable() that fields may use as sorts. z3_datatype_instance() instantiates one at concrete sorts.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
I <- z3_int_sort(ctx)
Tree <- z3_datatype(ctx, "Tree",
  leaf = list(),
  node = list(left = "Tree", value = I, right = "Tree"))
t <- z3_const(ctx, "t", Tree$sort)
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, Tree$is_node(t), Tree$value(t) == 7, Tree$is_node(Tree$left(t)))
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_eval(z3_model(s), t)
#> <z3_expr Tree> (node (node leaf 2 leaf) 7 leaf)

Color <- z3_enum_sort(ctx, "Color", c("red", "green", "blue"))
c1 <- z3_const(ctx, "c1", Color$sort)
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, c1 != Color$red, c1 != Color$green)
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_eval(z3_model(s), c1)
#> <z3_expr Color> blue

Point <- z3_datatype(ctx, "Point", Point = list(x = I, y = I))
tf <- z3_tuple_fields(Point)
names(tf$fields)
#> [1] "x" "y"
z3_simplify(tf$fields$y(tf$constructor(1, 2)))
#> <z3_expr Int> 2
